runs.narrative:
As of late, I found myself wandering through the decaying remnants of a once-vibrant estate. Initially, my exploration began in the nursery, where the dry compost under cracked glass hinted at negligence. Armed with a trowel and twine that I picked up, I ventured north to the furnace, its cold iron long dead and inert, underscoring the chill in the air.

Continuing my journey, I moved eastward to the fernery, its fronds brown and lifeless. The shears I collected there suggested an attempt to revive the place, yet the outcome was bleak. Pursuing this path of exploration, I took the token of age from the twine, a physical reminder of the time that has passed.

Navigating further east, I entered the vault, a space ordered yet abandoned, where I found a ledger. The drawers pulled open wide spoke of an inventory taken, perhaps in a futile attempt to catalogue what remained. Holding onto this ledger, I retraced my steps south through the colonnade, always guided by the necessity to document everything meticulously.

I arrived here with a trowel in hand, looking to revitalize the barren nursery. I took a lantern, hoping its light would guide me through the dim spaces, and shears, suspecting they might be useful for pruning or securing. As I navigated through the darkened corridors, I soon found myself in the cloche, where I discovered some withered plants. My instinct was to nurture them, so I carefully cut them, placing them into a basket I also found along my journey. Seeking a better environment for them, I climbed back up through the structure, passing through the colonnade, where the pillars seemed to hold stories of neglect and time.

Eventually, I returned to the nursery, but found myself contemplating the utility of a piece of twine that had caught my eye. Curiosity got the better of me; I tied it to the trowel, perhaps fantasizing about some makeshift tool improvement, but quickly realized it served no practical purpose and untied it just as swiftly. The twine then found its place on the ground from where it had come.
